text:
lisa: Quick question — can I add my domestic partner during open enrollment? We live together, share a lease and some joint accounts but we aren’t married. What counts as acceptable proof?
maya_peopleops: Yep you can add a domestic partner during open enrollment. We accept: joint lease/mortgage, 2 different months of joint utility or bank statements with both names, joint insurance policy, or a notarized domestic partner affidavit + one supporting doc.
lisa: Awesome, thanks. If I add them, will premiums come out pre-tax like spouse coverage?
sam_peopleops: Short answer: usually no. If your partner is not an IRS qualifying dependent, employer portion is treated as imputed income and employee-paid premiums are typically after-tax. We can run an estimate for your payroll impact.
lisa: Ugh ok — is there a way to enroll them as after-tax so they still get coverage?
maya_peopleops: Yes — choose the "domestic partner (after-tax)" option in the enrollment flow. You still need to upload the affidavit + one supporting doc. We'll mark it as after-tax on our side.
ben_hr: FYI if you elect partner coverage, payroll will flag imputed income and it may affect your tax withholding; payroll and benefits coordinate the entry.
tax-bot: Reminder: adding a non-dependent domestic partner often triggers imputed income per federal guidelines. State rules vary, so net take-home impact depends on your state withholding.
lisa: Good to know. Where do I upload the docs? Any naming conventions?
sam_peopleops: Upload via Workday -> Benefits -> "Upload eligibility docs". Preferred format: PDF. Filename example: lisa-dompartner-proof-2025.pdf. If you prefer, DM us the file and we can upload for you.
lisa: Uploaded the affidavit and lease just now. Also @maya_peopleops I included a note that partner has separate employer plan — does that affect anything?
maya_peopleops: If partner has their own employer plan, you can still add them here. It doesn't change eligibility but may affect coordination of benefits for claims. No paperwork extra from us besides the docs.
ben_hr: We'll review and verify within 2 business days. If anything's missing we'll ping you. Coverage effective date for open enrollment changes is Jan 1, 2026.
lisa: Thanks all — appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
